entities.summary:
Cleitus the White was a Macedonian public servant and commander of the Classical era, instrumental in the Hellenistic period. He served as a member of the Macedonian army and played a pivotal role in the reign of Alexander the Great. Cleitus was a trusted advisor to Alexander and was known for his bravery and military prowess.

As a public servant, Cleitus was responsible for the administration of various regions of the Macedonian Empire. He was a key figure in the distribution of land grants to veterans and was instrumental in the establishment of the city of Alexandria in Egypt.

Cleitus's legacy extended beyond his military campaigns and administrative roles. He was a patron of the arts and was known to have supported the works of prominent philosophers and poets. His commitment to the arts and sciences helped to shape the cultural landscape of the Hellenistic period.

Despite his significant contributions to the Macedonian Empire, Cleitus's life was cut short when he was killed in a feud with Alexander's successors. His death marked the end of an era and paved the way for the rise of the Seleucid Empire.

Cleitus's story is a testament to the enduring power of leadership and vision. His bravery, strategic thinking, and commitment to the arts and sciences have inspired generations of historians and scholars.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cleitus the White was a significant figure in the Hellenistic period, playing a key role in the establishment of the Macedonian Empire and the distribution of land grants to veterans. His legacy extended beyond his military campaigns and administrative roles, shaping the cultural landscape of the Hellenistic period.
